message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that:

| Requirement | How it’s satisfied |
|-------------|--------------------|
| **GPU** – NVIDIA RTX A6000 | `nvidia-tesla-a6000` |
| **OS** – Ubuntu 20.04 LTS | `ubuntu-os-cloud/ubuntu-2004-lts` |
| **Machine type** – 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM (adjust as needed) | `n1-standard-8` |
| **Zone** – e.g. `us-central1-a` | `us-central1-a` |
| **Project** – your GCP project ID | `my-gcp-project` |

> **⚠️ Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with the **Compute Engine API** enabled.  
> * You must have the **GPU quota** for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` in the chosen zone.  
> * You need a service account key or OAuth token with the `compute.instances.create` scope.  

---

## 1. Using the gcloud CLI

```bash
# Set variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --accelerator=type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

*The `startup.sh` script is optional; you can omit it if you don’t need custom startup commands.*

---

## 2. Using the REST API (curl)

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"

# Get the latest image ID
IMAGE_ID=$(curl -s \
  "https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${IMAGE_PROJECT}/global/images/family/${IMAGE_FAMILY}" \
  | jq -r .selfLink)

# Build the JSON payload
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON <<EOF
{
  "name": "${INSTANCE_NAME}",
  "machineType": "zones/${ZONE}/machineTypes/${MACHINE_TYPE}",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "${IMAGE_ID}",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/${ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": ${GPU_COUNT},
      "acceleratorType": "zones/${ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/${GPU_TYPE}"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
EOF

# Make the API call
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT}/zones/${ZONE}/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_JSON"
```

> **Note**:  
> * Replace `my-gcp-project` with your actual project ID.  
> * The `jq` command extracts the image link; install it if you don’t have it (`sudo apt-get install jq`).  
> * The `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` command fetches an OAuth token for the default credentials.  
> * If you’re using a service account key file, replace the `Authorization` header with `-H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /path/to/key.json | jq -r .access_token)"`.

---

## 3. Quick sanity check

After the instance is created, you can verify the GPU attachment:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --format="json(accelerators)"
```

You should see something like:

```json
{
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### TL;DR

- **CLI**: `gcloud compute instances create ... --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1`
- **REST**: POST to `https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances` with a JSON body that includes `"accelerators": [{"acceleratorCount":1,"acceleratorType":"zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"}]`.

Happy GPU computing! 🚀
